piece.name: Cakewalk Strut
piece.title: Cakewalk Strut
piece.notes: Test piece for cakewalk syncopation. First draft used rhythm:'pattern' with a hand-authored 3+3+2 onset grid -- but generator.py confirmed rhythm:'pattern' always couples bass to the identical onset grid (bypassing bass_style dispatch entirely, per bass.py's rhythm_events_override path), which would have made bass syncopate in unison with the melody instead of staying steady underneath it -- the opposite of the intended effect. Fixed by using rhythm:'free' + groove:'broken', the engine's own built-in 3+3+2 tresillo template (its docstring literally says 'Afro-Cuban tresillo' -- same rhythmic lineage as cakewalk). groove only threads into melody's own generation path; bass_style keeps running its own independent dispatch untouched, so root_fifth/pulse/root_only actually stay steady and on the beat as designed. swing stays 0.0 throughout -- cakewalk/ragtime syncopation is straight eighths with shifted accents, not a triplet shuffle. ABA form (intro, strain A, strain B, strain A reprise, outro) mirrors real published cakewalk sheet music structure. One counterpoint voice in strain B only, for a light countermelody.

sections.name: intro
sections.notes: Vamp -- establishes the steady march pulse before the syncopated tune enters properly in strain A.

sections.name: strain_a
sections.notes: Main strain. root_fifth bass stays flatly on the beat while the melody's 3+3+2 grouping cuts across it -- that tension is the actual cakewalk effect, not a trick layered on top of it.

sections.name: strain_b
sections.notes: Contrasting strain -- bass moves to pulse for a touch more insistence, still steady/unsyncopated. One light countermelody above, the way a period brass-band arrangement might carry a second voice.

sections.name: strain_a_reprise
sections.notes: Return of strain A -- classic ABA parlor-piece structure. No counterpoint here, mirrors the original strain's simplicity.
